findings.claim: The ledger routes this whole mixed source node only to ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4 as generic finite image classification. Its statement also contains dihedral modularity at the Serre weight/level and a bad-dihedral weight calculation. Neither nonclassification component receives an explicit source-linked owner/phase in this row. The general mixed-node preservation rule does not identify the component destinations; applying this row literally assigns modularity to the early image owner, while reading it as classification-only leaves the other clauses unrouted.
findings.evidence: The retained data/decompositions/ClassicalSerreModularity.json node includes KW I Lemma 6.2(i) and (ii). Independently retrieved https://math.ucla.edu/~shekhar/papers/results.pdf (SHA256 3c389dc33e09fe847f5d8189ffd8915b5c1a73424e64e4fed6769829883bad82), pp. 10-11: Lemma 6.1 is group classification, while 6.2(i) says Then rho-bar is modular and gives exact weight/level, using Serre/Wiese for p=2; 6.2(ii) uses the Serre weight definition. Independently read https://arxiv.org/pdf/2108.07577v2 (SHA256 0c6850dafda032f7a4008947c519b5aef8cc13762207bb67c36810170a8eebe6), Lemma 1.14 pp. 8-9 and proof: distinct niveau-one/two weight calculations follow the image result. Current R01.4 owns image/oddness theory, R17.5/R17.6 own soluble modularity, R15.4 owns the weight recipe, and R20.5 retains the assigned Wiese/conditional refinement. This is a migration defect, not an allegation that the source theorem is false or that the current stage graph contains a cycle.
